chapter_theme: Joining and going (கலவு செலவு): the soul's passage from the kevala condition, through the sakala, to removal of the bonds ends in the pure state beyond waking; give up anger, direct the mind, and rest in grace, and even stone splits into open space.

2302.reading: Joining in the kevala condition, going in the sakala, and the removal that comes as they leave: when one sees oneself spread through these, the three cease to spread, and in the faultless waking-beyond there is purity.
2302.nuance: கேவலம், சகலம் and சுத்தம் are the soul's three conditions in Siddhanta: alone with its mala, embodied, and pure. Whether மூன்றும் is these three conditions or the three malas is not settled by the verse.

2303.reading: While you can still win, let go of anger; as far as it will go, direct this mind; if night and day you rest in grace, even stone will split open and become the vast space.
2303.nuance: வெல்லும் அளவில் (while you can prevail) puts the test of giving up anger where it has power, as the Kural does. தூங்கினால் (if you sleep, or rest, or hang on) may point to yogic sleep in grace. கல் may be the hard heart, and கடுவெளி the open space taken as Siva's. Sengalvaraya notes a near-parallel line in Kandar Alankaram 15.

links.note: Both place the giving up of anger where one has the power to act on it: the Kural says restraint counts only where anger can take effect, Tirumular says let it go while you can still win.

2302 says that when one sees oneself (தனைக்கண்டால்) spread through the kevala, sakala and leaving conditions, the three cease and purity (சுத்தமே) follows; 2237 says that within the suddha state, beyond kevala, one knows oneself by oneself (தன்பால் தனையறி). Both make seeing oneself the mark of the pure state.

source_issues: 2303: line 2 reads செலுத்துமிஹ், a misprint for செலுத்துமின்.
